transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I just feel like I can’t sit still. Like, it’s not just being bored or fidgety once in a while. It feels like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to stay in one place, especially in the radiology suite or in class.

I’ll be trying to pay attention or just do what I’m supposed to do, but my body feels like it has to move. I end up shifting around constantly, standing up if I can, pacing when there’s any chance, or finding some excuse to go do something just so I’m not stuck sitting there. I’ve been trying to just tough it out for months, telling myself I should be able to handle it, but it hasn’t really gotten better. It’s just… uncomfortable, like this pressure building up when I’m still too long.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, especially antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or other psychiatric medications?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, not that I’m aware of. I haven’t recently started anything like that or had some dose change that lines up with this. I’m trying to think if there’s anything I’m forgetting, but nothing is coming to mind—no new psych meds or nausea meds or anything like that recently.
Thinking back, did you notice this kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's new for you as an adult?

No, it definitely isn’t new. I mean, it feels worse now because I’m in radiology training and I’m expected to be still and professional and all that, but when I think back, this was around when I was little too.

My parents still bring up elementary school conferences sometimes, like almost as a joke but also not really a joke, where teachers would tell them I was constantly out of my seat. Like I’d get up when I wasn’t supposed to, call out answers, or rush ahead before the teacher had even finished giving the directions. That was way before middle school. So yeah, it’s not like this just started as an adult or only because of the radiology program. It’s been kind of a long-running thing.
Aside from feeling physically restless, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or everyday matters—more days than not?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in that way, at least. I mean, I get stressed about stuff like anyone does, especially when there’s school or work expectations, but it doesn’t feel like I’m sitting around worrying about a bunch of different things all day.

It’s more like my body is the problem, if that makes sense. Like I’ll be in a situation where I’m supposed to sit still, and I’m not necessarily thinking, “Oh no, what if this happens, what if that happens,” it’s more just this internal pressure to move. I don’t really notice a constant worry loop about health or everyday stuff. At least… not that I’d describe as excessive.
Do you also notice trouble staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or often losing track of things and getting easily distracted, even outside of the restlessness we've talked about?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from the restlessness, honestly. Like, I don’t know if I’d say I’ve noticed some whole separate focus problem in the same way. A lot of the time when I lose track of something, it feels like it’s because I’m already uncomfortable sitting there or I’m needing to move, not necessarily because my mind just can’t stay on it.

I mean, I can get distracted like anyone, especially if something is boring or takes forever, but I don’t know that I’ve really been tracking it as its own issue. I haven’t sat down and thought, “Oh, I’m constantly losing things,” or “I can never follow details.” It’s more that the sitting still part is the thing that jumps out to me and gets noticed by other people.

So… maybe a little? But I’m not sure I can give you a confident yes on that. I’d probably need you to tell me what kinds of examples you mean, because I might not be thinking of it the right way.
Outside of times when you're feeling restless or need to move, do you often make careless mistakes, forget appointments or things you need to bring, or misplace items like your keys or phone?

Honestly, I’m not sure I can say yes to that in a clear way. Like, I do misplace my phone sometimes, but I feel like everybody does that, and I haven’t really noticed it being a major pattern for me. Same with appointments or bringing things—I don’t have this immediate list in my head of examples where I’m constantly forgetting stuff or getting in trouble because of it.

Careless mistakes… I guess I’d have to think more about what counts. If you mean like repeatedly missing details even when I’m calm and not fidgety or trying to leave the situation, I don’t know that I’ve noticed that as its own separate thing. I’m not saying it never happens, because I’m human, but it’s not something that stands out to me the way the sitting-still issue does.

So I guess my answer is: not really that I’ve noticed, or at least I’m not confident enough to say it’s often. If there are specific examples you’re thinking of, I might be able to answer better.
Would you say this restlessness and impulsiveness causes real problems for you not just at work or school, but also in your personal relationships or home life?

Yeah… I mean, the biggest place it’s become a real problem is definitely my program and clinicals. It’s not just “oh, I’m energetic” or people joking that I can’t sit still. My clinical evaluations have actually taken a hit because of it.

Supervisors have told me that the way I act—like being too keyed up, jumping in, moving around too much, not waiting my turn with the flow of things—can disrupt patient flow and make teamwork harder. And that was honestly really embarrassing to hear, because I don’t go in trying to make things harder for anyone. I’m trying to do well, and then I get feedback that my behavior is affecting the whole team.

It got serious enough that I was put on a formal remediation plan. So it’s not just in my head, and it’s not just one person being annoyed with me. It’s documented now, basically. And I’m worried that if I can’t get it under control, it could actually cost me my place in the program. That’s the part that scares me the most.

At home or with relationships… I don’t know if I can explain that as clearly. But in terms of real-life consequences, school and clinical training have definitely been affected in a pretty major way.
Aside from the restlessness and impulsivity, have you ever had ongoing problems with defiance, aggression, lying, stealing, or breaking rules—either as a child or now as an adult?

No, I don’t think so. Not in any kind of ongoing pattern, at least.

I mean, I’ve had moments where I’ve argued or gotten frustrated, especially if I felt like someone was telling me to slow down or stop doing something and I didn’t agree in the moment, but I wouldn’t describe myself as defiant in the sense of constantly refusing rules or trying to challenge authority. And aggression, lying, stealing, breaking rules… none of that really stands out to me as a thing in my childhood or now.

Like, I wasn’t the kid getting in trouble for hurting people or stealing stuff or purposely causing problems. If I got corrected, it was more about being too much or not waiting, not about being malicious or sneaky. And now as an adult, same thing—I’m not trying to break rules or get around them. If anything, I’m usually trying really hard to do things right, and then I mess up the way I come across.

So I guess my answer is no, not that I’m aware of.
